original_question: Suppose B is a subgroup of the symmetric group S_Ω on an infinite set Ω. Will the amalgamated free product S_Ω*_B S_Ω of two copies of S_Ω with amalgamation of B be embeddable in S_Ω? This is a weakened form of the group case of Question 4.4 in(G. M. Bergman, Indag. Math., 18(2007), 349–403). It is known that S_Ω*_B S_Ω need not be so embeddable by a map respecting B(Algebra Number Theory, 3(2009), 847–879, § 10).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.15 in the 21st issue of The Kourovka Notebook (page 163): the question whether, for a subgroup B of the full symmetric group S_Ω on an infinite set Ω, the amalgamated free product S_Ω *_B S_Ω is embeddable in S_Ω. The entry explicitly says this is a weakened form of the group case of Bergman’s Question 4.4.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the official target almost verbatim. It has the correct ambient group S_Ω on an infinite set Ω, the correct arbitrary subgroup B ≤ S_Ω, the correct group-theoretic construction S_Ω *_B S_Ω, and the correct contextual point that this is weaker than Bergman’s earlier 'over B' amalgamation question. It also correctly records the nearby remark that an embedding respecting the given copy of B is known to fail in general.
missing_details: Make the quantifiers explicit: the question is for every infinite set Ω and every subgroup B ≤ Sym(Ω).
Spell out that S_Ω denotes the full symmetric group Sym(Ω) on Ω.
Specify that S_Ω *_B S_Ω is the amalgamated free product in the category/variety of all groups, with the two copies of B identified via the given inclusions B ↪ S_Ω.
Replace 'embeddable in S_Ω' by the explicit condition 'there exists an injective group homomorphism S_Ω *_B S_Ω → S_Ω'.
State explicitly that, unlike Bergman’s original Question 4.4, no requirement is imposed that the embedding be over B, i.e. agree with the prescribed copy of B inside S_Ω.
refined_question: For every infinite set Ω, let S_Ω = Sym(Ω) be the full symmetric group on Ω, and let B be an arbitrary subgroup of S_Ω. Form the amalgamated free product S_Ω *_B S_Ω in the category of groups, where the two factors are amalgamated along the common subgroup B via the given inclusions B ↪ S_Ω. Must there exist an injective group homomorphism S_Ω *_B S_Ω → S_Ω? Here the embedding is asked for only as an abstract group embedding into S_Ω, not necessarily one that is over B.
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Problem 21.15, not the broader neighboring problem 17.22. Problem 21.15 is explicitly described there as a weakened form of the group case of Bergman’s Question 4.4. The main hidden point that must be made explicit in a stand-alone rewrite is the distinction between an abstract embedding into S_Ω and an embedding 'over B': the notebook immediately notes that the stronger over-B version is already known to fail, so the refined question should preserve the weaker formulation and state that absence of an over-B requirement clearly.
